top_temples.name: Kapileshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ancient Shiva shrine in Belgaum, known as 'Kashi of the South'; inscriptions near Kamal Basti date it to around 1000 AD.

top_temples.name: Military Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Camp Road, Belgaum; built and maintained by the Indian Army, one of the city's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Kalameshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located in Old Belgaum, draws devotees despite being outside the main city area.

top_temples.name: Hooli Panchalingeshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Belgaum district; Chalukya-era temple protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

top_temples.name: Saundatti Yellamma Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Saundatti, about 78 km from Belgaum city; one of Karnataka's most visited Devi shrines.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Bangalore (Sri Radha Krishna Chandra Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Rajajinagar, North Bengaluru; considered the largest ISKCON temple in Karnataka.

top_temples.name: Dodda Basavana Gudi (Bull Temple)
top_temples.location_note: South Bengaluru; built 1537 by Kempe Gowda, houses one of the largest Nandi monoliths in the world.

top_temples.name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built into a natural cave by Kempe Gowda I in the 16th century, in Gavipuram.

top_temples.name: Chokkanathaswamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Domlur, near the airport; 10th-century Chola-era structure, one of the city's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Sri Someshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ulsoor; originally Chola-built, later renovated by the Vijayanagara Empire.

top_temples.name: Adumalleshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 5 km from Chitradurga; cave temple in a natural rocky cavern with the Nandi Teertha spring.

top_temples.name: Hidimbeshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: On hilltops above Chitradurga town; Chalukya-era construction with Hoysala-style carvings.

top_temples.name: Nayakanahatti Thipperudraswamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 35 km from Chitradurga; honors sage Thipperudraswamy, major annual Phalguna festival.

top_temples.name: Holalkere Ganesha Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Holalkere taluk of Chitradurga district; established in 1475 CE by a local Palegar chieftain.

top_temples.name: Halu Rameshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Hosadurga taluk of Chitradurga district; associated with Lord Rama's worship of Shiva.

top_temples.name: Sri Anjaneya Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Shamanur village, Davangere district; ancient temple believed to be about 800 years old.

top_temples.name: Bagali Kalleshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Harpanahalli, Davangere district; 9th-century Chalukyan temple with a carved Ugra Narasimha statue.

top_temples.name: Shri Durgambika Temple
top_temples.location_note: Davangere city; current structure built in 1932, idol brought from Dugatti village.

top_temples.name: Eshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Davangere district; noted for Hoysala-style architecture and Gajalakshmi carvings.

top_temples.name: Harihareshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: In nearby Harihar town on the Tungabhadra river, part of Davangere district.

top_temples.name: Sri Manjunatha Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: The town's central shrine; a major multi-faith pilgrimage site administered under a unique Jain-Hindu tradition.

top_temples.name: Bahubali (Gommateshwara) Statue Shrine
top_temples.location_note: 39-ft monolithic statue erected in 1980 on a hill within the Dharmasthala temple complex, reflecting its Jain heritage; treated here as a subsidiary shrine of the same complex rather than a fully separate temple.

top_temples.name: Mahabaleshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Founded by Kadamba king Mayurasharma in the 4th century; often called 'Dakshina Kashi', second in sanctity only to Varanasi's Kashi Vishwanath.

top_temples.name: Maha Ganapati Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located near the Mahabaleshwar Temple; tradition holds devotees should seek Ganesha's blessing before visiting Mahabaleshwar.

top_temples.name: Hoysaleswara Temple
top_temples.location_note: 12th-century Hoysala masterpiece with twin shrines and about a thousand carved wall figures; UNESCO World Heritage Site.

top_temples.name: Kedareshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Trikutachala-style temple built in 1219 by Hoysala king Ballala II and queen Abhinava Ketala Devi, near Hoysaleswara.

top_temples.name: Virupaksha Temple
top_temples.location_note: Dates to the 7th century; one of the oldest continuously functioning temples in India, UNESCO World Heritage Site.

top_temples.name: Vittala Temple
top_temples.location_note: Famed for its stone chariot and musical pillars; a centerpiece of the Hampi UNESCO complex.

top_temples.name: Chandramouleshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 700 years old, in the Hubli-Dharwad twin city, noted for its hybrid architectural style.

top_temples.name: Siddharoodha Math
top_temples.location_note: Hubli; samadhi shrine of the revered saint Siddharoodha Swamiji, an active pilgrimage math.

top_temples.name: Nuggikeri Hanumantha Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the region's most popular shrines, drawing large crowds on Saturdays and Hanuman Jayanti.

top_temples.name: Trinetra Shri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
top_temples.location_note: Gokul Road area of Hubli; a relatively modern temple.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Sri Krishna Balarama Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hubli; known for its serene grounds and Vaishnava teaching activities.

top_temples.name: Kotilingeshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kammasandra village, Kolar district; houses a 108-foot monolithic granite Shiva linga, among the tallest in Asia, established 1980.

top_temples.name: Kolaramma Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kolar town; built by the Gangas and renovated by the Cholas, classic Dravidian style.

top_temples.name: Someshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 60 km from Kolar; 14th-century temple recognized as a protected national monument.

top_temples.name: Sri Kashi Vishweshwara Temple (Antaragange)
top_temples.location_note: At the base of Antaragange hill near Kolar; features a natural spring flowing from a stone Nandi's mouth.

top_temples.name: Venkataramana Temple
top_temples.location_note: Guttahalli village, about 29 km from Kolar; modeled on the Tirupati Venkateswara temple.

top_temples.name: Sri Mookambika Temple
top_temples.location_note: In the Western Ghat foothills; one of the seven Mukti Kshetras, associated with Adi Shankaracharya who is said to have consecrated the idol.

top_temples.name: Ganapathi Sub-shrine, Mookambika Temple Complex
top_temples.location_note: A subsidiary shrine within the Mookambika temple complex (alongside other sub-shrines to Shiva, Vishnu, Subrahmanya and Naga deities); noted here as no separate standalone major temple exists in Kollur town besides Mookambika itself.

top_temples.name: Kukke Sri Subrahmanya Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Kumaradhara river; one of Karnataka's most visited pilgrimage temples, famed for Naga Pratishtha and Sarpa Samskara rituals.

top_temples.name: Adi Subrahmanya Temple
top_temples.deity: Subrahmanya (in serpent form, Vasuki and Adishesha)
top_temples.location_note: Located immediately next to the main Kukke Subrahmanya Temple; site of two sacred anthills.

top_temples.name: Kadri Manjunatheshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Among the oldest temples in South India, dating to the 10th-11th century; houses a bronze Lokeshwara idol.

top_temples.name: Kudroli Gokarnanatheshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Founded 1912, remodeled in 1991 in Chola gopuram style; one of Mangalore's most-visited temples.

top_temples.name: Mangaladevi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bolara, about 3 km southwest of city centre; the temple after which Mangalore is named.

top_temples.name: Sharavu Mahaganapathi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Central Mangalore; one of the city's most well-known pilgrimage stops.

top_temples.name: Kateel Durga Parameshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: On an islet in the Nandini river near Mangalore; noted for its riverine setting.

top_temples.name: Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Melkote's principal shrine; closely associated with the Vaishnava saint Ramanujacharya, a major pilgrimage centre in Mandya district.

top_temples.name: Yoganarasimha Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Yoga Narasimha hill in Melkote; 12th-century Hoysala-period temple with intricate carvings.

top_temples.name: Murudeshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Kanduka Giri hill overlooking the Arabian Sea; features one of the world's tallest Shiva statues (123 ft) and a tall gopura.

top_temples.name: Ganapathi and Subramaniyar Sub-shrines, Murudeshwara Temple Complex
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrines within the same Murudeshwara temple complex; used here as the town's second temple entry since no separate major standalone temple exists within Murudeshwar itself.

top_temples.name: Chamundeshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Chamundi Hill, Mysore; one of the 18 Mahashakti Peethas, reached via a 1,000-step climb.

top_temples.name: Chennakesava Temple, Somanathapura
top_temples.location_note: On the Kaveri river near Mysore; celebrated Hoysala-era temple with detailed narrative carvings.

top_temples.name: Someswara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Just north of Mysore Palace; built by the Wodeyars in the 13th century, has three shrines.

top_temples.name: Sri Bhuvaneshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Within the Mysore Palace complex; dedicated to the goddess as creator of the universe.

top_temples.name: Mallikarjuna Temple
top_temples.location_note: Mysore; ancient temple known for its architecture and historical significance.

top_temples.name: Kedareshvara Temple, Balligavi
top_temples.location_note: Near Shikaripura, about an hour from Shimoga; 11th-century Chalukya temple with 12th-century Hoysala additions.

top_temples.name: Aghoreshvara Temple, Ikkeri
top_temples.location_note: About 30 minutes from Shimoga; 16th-century temple, a major Keladi Nayaka-era monument.

top_temples.name: Rameshwara Temple, Keladi
top_temples.location_note: Near Ikkeri, about 30 minutes from Shimoga; 16th-century temple tied to the historic Keladi kingdom.

top_temples.name: Shiva Temple, Shimoga
top_temples.location_note: Within Shimoga city; known for its architecture and quiet setting.

top_temples.name: Sigandur Chowdeshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Sharavathi backwaters, Shimoga district; draws large daily crowds of pilgrims.

top_temples.name: Sringeri Sharada Peetham (Sharadamba Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Seat established by Adi Shankaracharya; one of the four cardinal mathas of Advaita Vedanta, on the Tunga river.

top_temples.name: Vidyashankara Temple
top_temples.location_note: 14th-century temple in Sringeri known for its Vijayanagara-style architecture and 12 zodiac pillars.

top_temples.name: Goravanahalli Mahalakshmi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Koratagere taluk, about 30 km from Tumkur; idol regarded as self-manifested (swayambhu), draws large crowds statewide.

top_temples.name: Kalleshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in the 9th century by the Nolamba Dynasty, Tumkur district.

top_temples.name: Siddhalingeshwara Temple, Yediyur
top_temples.location_note: Yediyur, Tumkur district; well-known pilgrim site with an associated natural spring, Siddhaganga.

top_temples.name: Chennakeshava Temple, Kaidala
top_temples.location_note: Kaidala, Tumkur district; blends Vijayanagara and Hoysala architectural styles.

top_temples.name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
top_temples.location_note: Tumkur; built by Kanthirava Narasaraja I, later renovated by Mysore king Krishnaraja Wodeyar III in 1858.

top_temples.name: Sri Krishna Matha
top_temples.location_note: Udupi's defining shrine, founded by the philosopher-saint Madhvacharya; famous for its Kanakana Kindi window ritual.

top_temples.name: Anantheshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Adjacent to Sri Krishna Matha; over 1,000 years old, Chalukyan-style architecture, linked to the Alupa dynasty.

top_temples.name: Chandramouleshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Anantheshwara Temple in Udupi; legend ties it to the Moon God's worship of Shiva here.

top_temples.name: Anegudde Vinayaka Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kumbhashi, about 25 km from Udupi; popular Ganesha shrine on the route between Udupi and Murudeshwar.

top_temples.name: Shri Vishweshwara Temple, Yellur
top_temples.location_note: Yellur village, Udupi district; over 1,000 years old, mentioned in historical rock inscriptions.
